question: The temperature at which an oil starts to burn, leading to a burnt flavour in the foods being prepared is called:
solution:
The correct answer is __**smoke point**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• The smoke point is the temperature at which an oil or fat begins to visibly smoke and break down, producing a burnt flavor and potentially harmful compounds.
 
• It is an important factor in cooking and frying, as heating an oil beyond its smoke point can negatively affect the taste and safety of the food.
 
• The smoke point varies depending on the type of oil or fat. For instance, refined oils generally have higher smoke points than unrefined oils.
 
• Common cooking oils and their approximate smoke points: Canola oil (~400°F/204°C), Olive oil (~375°F/190°C), and Avocado oil (~520°F/271°C).
 
• Oils with higher smoke points are suitable for high-temperature cooking methods like deep-frying, while oils with lower smoke points are better for dressings and low-heat cooking.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Boiling Point:** The temperature at which a liquid turns into vapor. Unlike the smoke point, the boiling point is not a relevant factor for cooking oils.
 
• **Ignition Temperature:** The minimum temperature at which a substance catches fire without an external flame or spark. This is much higher than the smoke point.
 
• **Critical Temperature:** The temperature above which a gas cannot be liquefied, regardless of pressure. This term is not related to cooking oils.
 
• **Refined vs. Unrefined Oils:** Refining removes impurities, increasing the smoke point of oils. For example, refined coconut oil has a smoke point of ~450°F, while unrefined coconut oil smokes at ~350°F.
 
• **Health Implications:** Overheating oils beyond their smoke point can degrade nutrients and produce harmful compounds like acrolein, which is linked to respiratory and health issues.
